subject: Correct cross choice for three parent population

messages.author: 5d5dfb7aab7ae4fd
messages.subject: Correct cross choice for three parent population
parts:
I am new at using R/qtl2 and have a question regarding the correct cross choice for a population derived from three parents. I have an F6 population derived from three parents.

I have successfully been able to load data for an F2-intercross with the following .yaml file:
#Header
crosstype: f2
geno: geno.csv
founder_geno: parentalgeno.csv
pheno: pheno.csv
covar: covar.csv
phenocovar: phenocovar.csv
gmap: gmap.csv
alleles:
- A
- B
genotypes:
  AA: 1
  AB: 2
  BB: 3
na.strings:
- '-'
- NA

Will the F2-intercross take the founder_geno file into consideration when performing downstream analyses? 

I am concerned that F2 is not the most appropriate choice for my data. I believe HS may be a better choice, however, when I attempt to use the Heterogeneous Stock it seems that the input is constrained to having 8 parents according to the documentation. It may be why I'm getting this error:
Error in read_cross2("fixedHA467_20.yaml") :
length(alleles) [2] != expected number [8]
but I'm confused as to why it is referring to alleles rather than parents.


Is there a way to get HS to work with three parents or is there a better choice for cross type to be using with my data?

Thank you for your help with this.

Cloe

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Correct cross choice for three parent population
parts:
There's a cross type "ail3" that should work. It needs the founder genotypes for the 3 founder lines. The cross info is a single integer with the number of generations for each individual (6 for all individuals, in your case).

I wouldn't treat these as an F2. And yes, cross type "hs" is specifically 8 founders.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Correct cross choice for three parent population
parts:
1. I can't tell what's going on with the cross info. My example looks much like that. If you email your data to me privately, I can try to figure out what's going wrong.

When the cross is read into R, type mycross$cross_info (replacing "mycross" with the name of the object you created). What do you get?

2. Currently we just have "ail" for 2-way AILs and "ail3" for 3-way AILs. Well, also "hs" which is basically an 8-way AIL.

3. The three alleles are the labels that will be used for the 3 parental/founder lines.

karl
